title: Tale of the Ensorcelled Prince

full_text:
When the fisherman convinced the Jinni to grant him true fortune, the spirit led him to an isolated valley nestled between four mysterious hills. In the center lay a shimmering lake whose waters teemed with fish of four distinct colors: white, red, blue, and yellow. The Jinni commanded the fisherman to cast his net once, take the catch to the Sultan of the city, and never fish there more than once a day.

The fisherman caught four magnificent fish and presented them to the Sultan, who rewarded him with four hundred pieces of gold. But when the royal cook placed the fish into a copper frying pan, the wall of the kitchen opened, and a maiden of supernatural beauty emerged, tapped the pan with a wand of bamboo, and overturned the fish into the coals before vanishing. Astounded, the Sultan resolved to uncover the secret of the four-colored fish himself.

Riding alone into the wilderness, the Sultan discovered a magnificent palace built of polished black marble, surrounded by silent gardens. Entering its deserted halls, he heard the faint sound of groaning. Following the voice, he drew back a tapestry and beheld a handsome young prince sitting upon a raised dais. When the Sultan bade him rise, the youth lifted his robe, revealing with tears that from his waist to his feet he was transformed into solid black stone.

The prince recounted his tragic history: he had been the rightful monarch of the Four Islands, but his treacherous queen, an adept in dark sorcery, had overthrown his throne, turned him half to stone, transformed his loyal citizens into fish of four colors according to their four original quarters, and turned his four majestic hills into an enchanted wilderness.

Moved to profound pity, the Sultan devised a daring plan. In the dead of night, he crept into the sorceress's secret pavilion, overpowered her champion, and disguised himself in the champion's garments. When the sorceress approached, the Sultan mimicked her confidant's voice and commanded her to break the enchantment upon the prince and the four islands before she could receive his favor. Deceived by love and fear, the sorceress sprinkled enchanted water, restoring the stone prince to flesh and blood, and transforming the lake back into a thriving, joyful city. The Sultan then struck down the sorceress, adopted the brave prince as his own son, and made the humble fisherman the chief treasurer of his realm.
moral: Perseverance against tyranny and cruelty will ultimately liberate the oppressed and restore stolen joy.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tale of the Ensorcelled Prince"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
